facts.value: Derives Fighter from gobj, reads fp->input.lstick[0].y and p_ftCommonData->x90, and compares the former with the negation of the latter. If the strict comparison succeeds, forwards the same gobj to fn_800D62C4 and returns true after that entry routine returns; otherwise returns false without dispatch.

evidence.why: Strict comparison controls the normal entry wrapper and all failure cases return false.

facts.rationale: States the precise indexed boundary and exceptional-float behavior without assuming valid controller/configuration ranges.
facts.value: Enters SquatWait through the Ft_MF_None/true wrapper only when fp->input.lstick[0].y < -p_ftCommonData->x90. Equality and greater values fail; under ordinary IEEE comparisons NaN in either operand also fails. This is a level test with no edge, duration, finite-value, sign-of-threshold or ground-state validation. The false path makes no state-entry call.

facts.value: Tries ftCo_800D68C0, ftCo_Attack100_CheckInput, ftCo_AttackS4_CheckInput, ftCo_AttackHi4_CheckInput, ftCo_AttackLw4_CheckInput, ftCo_AttackS3_CheckInput, ftCo_AttackHi3_CheckInput, ftCo_AttackLw3_CheckInput, ftCo_Attack1_CheckInput, ftCo_80091A4C, ftCo_800DE9D8, ftCo_Jump_CheckInput, ftCo_80099F9C, ftCo_Dash_CheckInput, and ftCo_SquatRv_CheckInput in exactly that order. Each receives the same gobj; the first true result returns immediately and suppresses later calls. The first two helpers dispatch non-NULL ftData_SpecialLw and ftData_SpecialHi entries when x687 and x686 respectively equal zero. Despite its name, the second is not the rapid-jab predicate. If all fail, this callback adds no transition.

facts.rationale: Replaces erroneous rapid-jab mapping with active callback-table and callee-table evidence, while preserving unresolved helper meanings.
facts.value: Implements action selection while sustained crouch is active. Its first two candidates dispatch the fighter-kind SpecialLw and SpecialHi tables, followed by the canonical smash, tilt, Attack1, common address-named, jump, dash and SquatRv checks in fixed priority. The ftCo_Attack100_CheckInput call must not be labeled rapid jab: its actual consumer is ftData_SpecialHi. Exact gameplay meanings of the remaining address-named checks are not established here.

evidence.why: All completion, setter, sentinel, weighted selection and retry branches.

facts.rationale: Preserves normal behavior while adding sentinel, optional animation and nontermination boundaries omitted by baseline.
facts.value: Delegates to ftCo_8008A7A8 with ft_data->x28. While frames remain the helper does nothing. On completion, a NULL table or a held item on a fighter other than Mewtwo/Fox requests current-animation restart; the setter is a no-op for ID -1. Otherwise a 1..100 random draw selects the first cumulative-weight bucket covering it, with assertion on sentinel exhaustion. Selection retries an immediate repeat unless current anim_id is 2 or 31, so invalid single-choice data can loop indefinitely. Selected IDs other than -1 install animation metadata, blend and script state; the animation-start call requires x590 != NULL. No local bounds or table-validity checks prove that all runtime data terminates safely.

evidence.why: Complete owned data flow and absence of allocation/ownership operations.
Physics follow-up clears shield-hit position-skip flag.

facts.rationale: Refines the retained TU data-flow overview with verified initialization and physics follow-up effects rather than inferred aliases.
facts.value: Entry reads indexed left-stick Y, the negated x90 threshold, optional held-item motion metadata, fighter kind and, only on the input-entry variant, x5F0. Both variants select SquatWait with animation operands 0.0F/1.0F/0.0F. Ft_MF_None permits Fighter_ChangeMotionState to clear x209A, then ftCommon_8007EFC0 writes x5F0 to it; Ft_MF_SkipNametagVis avoids that clear and the false selector omits the write. Animation forwards ft_data->x28, IASA forwards gobj through ordered predicates, physics applies friction/movement then clears shield_hit.skip_update_pos, and collision forwards gobj through position synchronization and a conditional Fall call. Objects and metadata are borrowed; this TU performs no allocation or ownership transfer.
